To find the rank of $A,$ we first reduce it to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 3 & -2 \\ 6 & -2 & -7 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 & -3 \\ 0 & -3 & -6 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 & -3 \\ 0 & -3 & -6 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & -3 & -6 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{4} & :={R}_{4}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix has $3$ pivot columns (or alternatively, it has exactly $3$ non-zero rows).

Therefore, $\text{rank}(A)=3.$
